symptoms.title: Pressing the trigger does nothing
symptoms.intro: No recording starts. Work through the likely causes below.

fix.macos: Whispy reads the trigger key through a listen-only event tap, which needs Input Monitoring. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring, enable Whispy V2, then restart it from the menu bar (Restart). Until then the menu says « The trigger key is not available… ».
Open /Applications/Whispy V2.app: its waveform appears in the menu bar. If it quits again, read ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log.
fix.linux: Start it with systemctl --user start whispy2 (or the switch in the Omarchy panel), then check whispy2 send status. If it stops again, read journalctl --user -u whispy2 -e and ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log.

fix.macos: At first launch Whispy downloads about 1.2 GB of models; the menu says Ready when you can dictate.
fix.linux: At first launch Whispy downloads about 1.2 GB of models. whispy2 send status shows "models_loaded":true when you can dictate.

steps.title: No X server for the key (X11)

fix.linux: Under X11 Whispy listens to Right Ctrl through XInput 2 on your display. If the unit started without DISPLAY, Whispy says so in a notification and in whispy2 send status. From your graphical session, run systemctl --user import-environment DISPLAY XAUTHORITY, then systemctl --user restart whispy2. Under Wayland, see the Wayland entry below.

steps.text: Another key or mode is set. On macOS, press the key shown in Settings → Trigger (see trigger). In toggle mode (trigger_mode) a single press starts and a second press stops.

symptoms.title: Recording works but no text appears
symptoms.intro: Whispy records, but nothing is typed into the focused field.

fix.macos: Whispy pastes (⌘V) or types through System Events, which needs Accessibility. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, enable Whispy V2 and restart it. A pasted text stays on the clipboard meanwhile: paste it by hand.

If Whispy says « Microphone heard nothing », the default input device is muted or wrong. Pick the right one in System Settings → Sound → Input: Whispy opens the current default at each dictation. Check that Whispy V2 is allowed in Privacy & Security → Microphone.
fix.linux: If Whispy says « Microphone heard nothing », the default ALSA/PulseAudio/PipeWire input is muted or wrong. Pick the right one in your sound settings (or pactl set-default-source): Whispy opens the current default at each dictation.
Under Wayland Whispy types through the virtual-keyboard protocol. Hyprland and sway support it; GNOME does not. The log line of the dictation says the insertion failed.

steps.text: The clip was discarded. A press under 0.3 s, a near-silent clip, or one with under 0.20 s of detected voice is ignored on purpose. ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log has one line per dictation with its outcome. See why short clips are ignored.

symptoms.title: Text appears garbled / accents wrong
symptoms.intro: Words arrive, but characters are wrong or missing.

steps.text: Keyboard layout. On macOS, keep copy_to_clipboard on (the default): the text is pasted, so accents arrive intact whatever your layout. Typing key by key depends on the layout.

fix.linux: On Linux the text is typed one key at a time. An app that drops fast synthetic keys may lose some; dictate shorter passages, or report it with the app's name.

symptoms.title: Whispy doesn't start / no menu bar or tray icon

fix.macos: The control socket is a single-instance lock: a second Whispy finds the first one answering and exits. Look for its icon in the menu bar, or ask status on ~/.whispy/v2/control.sock.
fix.linux: The control socket is a single-instance lock: a second Whispy finds the first one answering and exits. whispy2 send status answers if one runs; systemctl --user status whispy2 shows whether it is the service.

fix.macos: Read ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log. Rebuild and reinstall with the one-line installer, or make reinstall from a checkout.
fix.linux: Read journalctl --user -u whispy2 -e and ~/.whispy/v2/whispy2.log. Rebuild and reinstall with the one-line installer, or make reinstall from a checkout.

symptoms.title: First dictation is slow or fails (models)
symptoms.intro: The first dictation after launch takes long, or Whispy says the models are missing.

fix.macos: Whispy downloads its models at first launch into ~/.whispy/models (about 1.2 GB, SHA-256 checked) and says so in a notification. Without network, it retries at the next launch. The log names the file that failed.
fix.linux: Whispy downloads its models at first launch into ~/.whispy/models (about 1.2 GB, SHA-256 checked) with curl. Without network, it retries at the next start (systemctl --user restart whispy2). The log names the file that failed.

symptoms.title: Linux: the trigger key does nothing under Wayland
symptoms.intro: Under Wayland no app may listen to a global key.

fix.linux: Bind a key of your compositor to whispy2 send start on press and whispy2 send stop on release (or whispy2 send toggle). On Omarchy, run omarchy-dictation-use whispy && hyprctl reload and pick the key in the Whispy bar panel. See Install.

steps.title: whispy2 is not on the binding's PATH

fix.linux: The installer puts whispy2 in ~/.local/bin. If your compositor's PATH lacks it, write the full path: ~/.local/bin/whispy2 send start.

symptoms.title: Linux: the tray icon does not show
symptoms.intro: Under X11 Whispy shows a tray icon (StatusNotifierItem).

steps.title: No tray host in the panel

fix.linux: The icon needs a StatusNotifierItem host in your panel (KDE, XFCE and most bars have one). Without it Whispy posts one notification, « Tray icon unavailable », and runs on without it: dictation still works. Under Wayland there is no tray icon; on Omarchy, the bar panel shows the state.
